newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates edge higher ahead of Fed/Buba.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates edge higher ahead of Fed/Buba.

text.p: Dutch money market rates headed higher on Friday as the market awaited next week's meeting of the U.S. Fed and the German Bundesbank.
"I do not expect a rate rise next week," said one dealer, adding the market would probably calm down then.
The Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) meets next Tuesday and the Bundesbank on Thursday.

Dealers saw guilder rates edging up further ahead of both meetings with bid and call prices for three-month deposits seen at 3.40-3.50 percent. Three-month deposits were trading at 3.38/46 percent on Friday afternoon.

Call money rates also rose several basis points and dealers said liquidity had been unevenly divided among participants today. "This morning's allocation (under the special advances pact) looked sufficient," said one.
He added a few banks had to fill their liquidity gap by borrowing at the central bank's marginal advances rate of 4.5 percent in recent days. "That tells the story really," he said.
Call money rates rose to between 3.31 and 3.37 percent bid today from a range of 3.25 -3.31 percent bid on Thursday.
The guilder was a little firmer versus the German mark, trading at 112.6325 per 100 marks compared to 112.65 on Thursday.
